unsupported_claims: Reuse avoids bias only when each reused sample follows the exact biased transition distribution and does not correlate successive walk steps - this goes along with the false premise and the paper says no such conditions.

Bias-free reuse is achieved by reusing alias tables or rejection-sampling outcomes within the same state, so each step is an exact draw from the node2vec distribution - not in the evidence and misdescribes how sample reuse works in node2vec.

Efficiency gains come from amortizing table-building cost across walks, provided reuse is restricted to identical transition states - the paper attributes efficiency to reusing walk samples across source nodes, not to this.
rationale: The answer accepts the false premise by supplying conditions under which node2vec's sample reuse is bias-free, whereas the paper says sample reuse can introduce some bias while greatly improving efficiency. It also invents mechanisms (alias-table reuse, rejection sampling) that the evidence does not support as the source of the efficiency gain.
